ranking.rationale: Best single-feature bet: it directly adds item-specific surface effects on top of the already validated request-context family, targets the two substantive weak tab slices (0: 13,726 rows; 6: 5,170 rows), has low leakage/runtime risk, and preserves the proven baseline training recipe. It is more directly relevant to candidate ordering than a context-only cross.

A compact, low-risk interaction with a credible mechanism: user preferences can differ by request surface, which the additive baseline cannot express. It is strongly related to the only positive feature-family screen and targets the high-volume weak tab-0 slice. Slightly behind c02 because user-by-tab can be sparse for infrequent users and has less direct item-ranking specificity.

Provides a broad interaction mechanism that includes useful user-item and item-context effects without new data or leakage. However, replacing the scorer greatly expands scope versus a single interaction, has medium runtime/implementation risk, weak direct empirical support, and can make any outcome harder to attribute under one scarce experiment.

Very cheap and protocol-aligned correction because the official primary includes nDCG@5 while current selection uses GAUC only. It is ranked below interaction features because it can overfit repeated checkpoint choice to the same validation set and has only a small plausible gain, but it is a strong operational fallback.

Video-by-hour is a focused, low-risk item-context interaction supported by the positive request-context screen and weak early-hour diagnostics. Evidence is weaker than for tab: the cited bad hours are smaller slices, and many hour deficits are diagnostic rather than evidence that item-time interactions will generalize.

Safe and inexpensive, but tab and hour are already active baseline fields, so this modest context-only cross is comparatively duplicative and lacks a direct candidate-specific ranking mechanism. The weak tab/hour slices are reused validation diagnostics, not independent proof that their cross is beneficial.

Narrow, training-only regularization has low leakage and runtime risk and is at least directionally motivated by poor sparse and medium-item top-rank metrics. Still, the proposed 1/sqrt(count) scaling is not empirically calibrated, and poor segment nDCG does not isolate video-ID overfitting as the cause.

A simpler direct-ranking objective than the other loss candidates and well aligned with within-user evaluation. Its evidence is mostly conceptual: the closest tested loss change, user-normalized BCE, reduced primary by 0.00452, and sampled broad user-history pairs may not optimize nDCG@5. Medium runtime and batching complexity further reduce scarce-experiment value.

Potentially targets the GAUC-versus-nDCG gap, but it is more complex and validation-tailored than c06. The lambda value, detached swap weighting, and nDCG@5 focus introduce several unvalidated choices, increasing validation-overfitting and implementation risk under a one-experiment budget.

Listwise competition is relevant to ranking, but complete per-user grouping, exclusion rules, and list normalization create the highest feasibility and optimization risk among loss-only proposals. It has low confidence and no direct evidence that its assumptions fit these mostly sparse or incomplete user impression groups.

The candidate is narrow, but it relies on causal state construction with medium leakage risk and directly conflicts with the negative historical user-author-affinity screen. Repeated same-video exposure may be too limited to materially affect global ranking, while implementation errors in temporal ordering would be costly.

Lowest-risk implementation but weakest hypothesis. There is no optimization diagnostic indicating that 0.01 is too high, the expected gain is smallest, and changing learning rate under fixed epoch/patience can simply underfit. It is best reserved as a post-failure control rather than the scarce primary experiment.
